articles.title: SUS Pet Santista: Famílias carentes podem ter atendimento gratuito | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta prevê consultas, exames, cirurgias, internações e medicamentos gratuitos. Texto foi encaminhado à Procuradoria da Câmara.
articles.summary: O projeto SUS Pet Santista prevê consultas, exames e cirurgias gratuitas para cães e gatos de famílias de baixa renda, protetores e animais de rua em Santos.
articles.body:
Bombeiros resgatam cachorro de rua que caiu no mar em Porto Seguro (imagem ilustrativa) — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Um projeto de lei propõe a criação do programa “SUS Pet Santista”, voltado para atender gratuitamente cães e gatos de famílias em situação de vulnerabilidade socioeconômica e animais em situação de rua em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo. A proposta ainda será votada pelos vereadores.

O projeto, apresentado pelo vereador Sérgio Santana (PL), quer ampliar o acesso a atendimentos veterinários gratuitos no município. A iniciativa incluiu a realização de exames, tratamentos, cirurgias, internações, medicamentos, vacinação, castração e atendimento de urgência e emergência.

Segundo ele, a execução do ‘SUS Pet Santista’ poderia ocorrer por meio da estrutura pública já existente, do credenciamento em clínicas particulares ou de parcerias com universidades e entidades. Veja quem teria acesso ao programa, conforme a proposta:

Moradores de Santos : tutores de cães e gatos inscritos no CadÚnico ou com renda familiar de até dois salários mínimos.

Protetores independentes: pessoas que atuam na proteção animal e estejam devidamente cadastradas perante o órgão municipal competente

ONGs e entidades: entidades voltadas à proteção animal devidamente cadastradas

Cães e gatos comunitários: animais comunitários ou em situação de rua.

O projeto ainda prevê o atendimento de animais resgatados em situações de abandono, calamidade, acidentes ou outras circunstâncias de vulnerabilidade, desde que encaminhados por órgãos públicos competentes ou entidades de proteção animal.

De acordo com Santana, a criação do programa contribui para a prevenção e o controle de zoonoses e doenças infectocontagiosas , que muitas vezes não são combatidas pela falta de acesso a tratamentos veterinários por tutores sem condições financeiras.

“Cuidar dos animais também é cuidar das pessoas, das famílias e da cidade”, destacou.

O projeto foi encaminhado à Procuradoria da Câmara, que deve avaliar a legalidade e a constitucionalidade da proposta. Se aprovado, a proposta será encaminhada para votação em plenários pelos vereadores.

articles.title: Arco-íris surge ao lado do Cristo Redentor durante mudança no tempo | G1
articles.standfirst: Frente fria provoca instabilidade, com previsão de até 150 mm de chuva em dois dias; período mais crítico deve ser entre a noite desta quarta e a manhã de quinta-feira.
articles.summary: Frente fria provoca instabilidade, com previsão de até 150 mm de chuva em dois dias; período mais crítico deve ser entre a noite desta quarta e a manhã de quinta-feira.
articles.body:
Arco íris na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Reprodução TV Globo

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Um arco-íris chamou a atenção de moradores do Rio de Janeiro na tarde desta quarta-feira (25), em meio à mudança do tempo na cidade. Uma imagem registrada nesta tarde mostra o fenômeno ao lado do Cristo Redentor, no alto do Corcovado, enquanto áreas da Região Metropolitana já enfrentavam chuva forte e registro de raios.

A instabilidade é provocada pela aproximação de uma frente fria, que deixa o estado em alerta para temporais e grandes volumes de chuva nesta quarta e também na quinta-feira (26).

Na Região Metropolitana, há registro de chuva forte e raios, inclusive na Baía de Guanabara. Também chove de forma moderada em Duque de Caxias e São João de Meriti, na Baixada Fluminense, e nos bairros da Penha, Méier e Tijuca, na Zona Norte do Rio.

A previsão é que as áreas de instabilidade avancem para outras regiões da capital nas próximas horas.

Arco íris duplo na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Adriana Malafaia

Frente fria chega a Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Reprodução TV Globo

Chuva atinge o RJ — Foto: Guilherme Wanderley

Rio de Janeiro tem alerta para temporais nesta quarta (25) e quinta (26) — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

Pancadas de chuva atingem o Méier, na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Reprodução

Somados os volumes previstos para quarta e quinta-feira, a chuva pode acumular entre 100 e 150 milímetros em diferentes regiões do estado . Na Costa Verde, os acumulados podem chegar a 180 milímetros.

O período mais crítico deve ocorrer entre a noite desta quarta e a manhã de quinta-feira, com possibilidade de raios e rajadas de vento em torno de 80 km/h.

“Tendo em vista os volumes previstos, o potencial é elevado para impactos como alagamentos de vias, transbordamento de rios, enxurradas e deslizamentos”, afirmou a meteorologista Hana Silveira.

A Defesa Civil de São Gonçalo emitiu um alerta severo para o risco de temporal no município . Em Niterói, a Defesa Civil também enviou um aviso sobre a possibilidade de chuva moderada a forte, acompanhada de raios e rajadas de vento.

Calor continua nesta quarta; temperatura cai na quinta

Apesar da chegada da chuva, o calor ainda predomina nesta quarta-feira. Na cidade do Rio, a temperatura máxima pode chegar a 38°C.

Na quinta-feira, a previsão é de temporais durante a madrugada e a manhã. A partir da tarde, a chuva perde intensidade, mas deve continuar frequente, contribuindo para o aumento dos acumulados. A temperatura máxima prevista é de 26°C.

Na sexta-feira (27), a chuva perde força em todo o estado e deve ser fraca na maior parte das regiões. No Norte Fluminense, ainda pode chover forte durante a madrugada, mas a intensidade diminui ao longo do dia.

Veja as recomendações em caso de chuva forte e raios

O Centro de Operações Rio (COR) orienta a população a redobrar os cuidados durante os temporais.

Redobre a atenção ao dirigir e mantenha os faróis acesos.

Permaneça em local seguro e evite áreas com alagamentos.

Não caminhe por áreas inundadas. A correnteza pode arrastar pessoas, e a água pode esconder buracos e objetos perigosos.

Não fique próximo à margem de rios e córregos.

Nunca tente atravessar de carro uma via alagada.

Evite locais abertos e a prática de esportes ao ar livre, especialmente no mar.

Não se abrigue debaixo de árvores ou de coberturas metálicas.

Evite ficar próximo a precipícios, encostas ou lugares altos sem proteção.

Se houver queda de árvore, fique atento à possibilidade de rompimento da rede elétrica, que pode provocar acidentes.

articles.title: Abastecimento de água em Campina Grande e 7 cidades para nesta quinta | G1
articles.standfirst: Interrupção começa às 8h para manutenção corretiva e preventiva no sistema operacional. Previsão é de que o abastecimento seja retomado gradativamente na sexta-feira (27).
articles.summary: O abastecimento de água em Campina Grande e sete cidades do Agreste será interrompido para manutenção da Cagepa nesta quinta (26), com retorno gradual na sexta-feira.

O abastecimento de água será interrompido em Campina Grande e em outros sete municípios do Agreste da Paraíba a partir das 8h desta quinta-feira (26). Veja os locais afetados no fim da reportagem.

articles.title: Chuva e ventania provocam estragos no Vale do Aço | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuva provocou alagamentos, destruiu a cobertura de uma quadra escolar e interditou vias em Coronel Fabriciano. Estimativa do prejuízo é do dono da loja atingida.
articles.summary: Chuva no Vale do Aço causa alagamentos, queda de árvores e destrói telhados em Coronel Fabriciano e Timóteo, deixando prejuízo de R$ 100 mil em loja de móveis.
articles.body:
Chuva forte e ventania causam alagamentos e estragos no Vale do Aço — Foto: Gracielle Sol / Inter TV dos Vales

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Uma chuva rápida, acompanhada de fortes rajadas de vento, provocou alagamentos e estragos em diferentes pontos de Coronel Fabriciano , no Vale do Aço, na tarde desta quarta-feira (25). O temporal também causou transtornos em Timóteo.

Em Coronel Fabriciano, a cobertura da quadra poliesportiva da Escola Estadual Alberto Giovannini, no bairro Giovannini, foi destruída pela força do vento. Parte de um muro próximo à quadra já havia caído anteriormente.

A região da antiga rodoviária, na Avenida Magalhães Pinto, voltou a ficar alagada. A água chegou a entrar em estabelecimentos comerciais nas proximidades do viaduto.

Uma estrutura metálica com telhas se desprendeu de um imóvel e atingiu parte da Avenida Magalhães Pinto. O trecho precisou ser interditado.

Na Rua Araruama, também no bairro Giovannini, um carro estacionado teve o vidro traseiro quebrado. Segundo as informações recebidas, o veículo pode ter sido atingido por tijolos que se desprenderam de uma estrutura.

Na BR-381, o trânsito ficou parado na altura do bairro Amaro Lanari, por causa de uma enxurrada de lama que desceu pelas margens da rodovia e atingiu a pista.

Em Timóteo, uma árvore caiu sobre a rede elétrica no bairro Vila dos Técnicos.

Empresário estima prejuízo superior a R$ 100 mil

A força do vento também destruiu o telhado e a fachada de uma loja de móveis na Avenida Magalhães Pinto. Toda a estrutura do telhado, incluindo a armação metálica, desabou sobre dois carros que estavam no local.

O empresário Ivair de Andrade estima que o prejuízo ultrapasse R$ 100 mil. Apesar dos danos, afirmou que os bens atingidos têm seguro.

Ele estima que os prejuízos ultrapassem R$ 100 mil. Apesar dos danos, afirmou que os bens atingidos possuem seguro.

“Derrubou meu telhado, derrubou a frente aqui toda da loja. Ninguém segura o vento, ninguém sabe a força que vai vir. Mas acima de 100 mil reais, tranquilamente. É, bem acima. Mas vai dar certo. Não, preocupa não que tudo tem seguro, a gente anda com tudo organizadinho”, disse.

Na Rua Araruama, a cobertura de um prédio foi arrancada pela força do vento. A estrutura foi lançada a quase 50 metros de distância e atingiu duas motocicletas na Avenida Magalhães Pinto.

Por causa da quantidade de telhas espalhadas pela pista, o trânsito precisou ser interditado no cruzamento da Rua Cabo Frio com a Avenida Magalhães Pinto, no sentido bairro. A Cemig desligou a energia elétrica no local.

Gabriel Cindino, funcionário da família proprietária do imóvel, contou que a queda da estrutura ocorreu por volta das 15h30. Segundo ele, a estrutura metálica se desprendeu da armação do prédio e caiu sobre a rede elétrica.

Ele afirmou que houve danos materiais, mas ninguém ficou ferido.

articles.summary: O engenheiro Daniel de Moraes Andrade substitui o general Rogério Cetrim de Siqueira na futura pasta de Secretaria de Reconstrução, Obras e Infraestrutura.
articles.body:
O engenheiro Daniel de Moraes Andrade (à direita) substitui o general Rogério Cetrim de Siqueira (à esquerda) na futura pasta de Secretaria de Reconstrução, Obras e Infraestrutura. — Foto: Mateus Raugust/Divulgação

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O secretariado Luciano Zucco ( PL ), governador eleito do Rio Grande do Sul, teve a primeira troca mesmo antes da nova gestão do Palácio Piratini. A mudança ocorre na Secretaria de Reconstrução, Obras e Infraestrutura , uma das 18 pastas confirmadas para o Executivo gaúcho a partir de 2027.

Segundo o governo eleito, o general Rogério Cetrim de Siqueira, inicialmente anunciado como secretário , comunicou nesta semana "impossibilidade de assumir o cargo em razão de questões de ordem pessoal e de saúde de sua esposa, que comprometeriam a dedicação integral exigida pela missão".

Assim, nesta quarta-feira (25), Zucco anunciou o nome do engenheiro civil e empresário Daniel de Moraes Andrade como futuro titular da pasta. O indicado foi secretário de Infraestrutura no governo Yeda Crusius (PSDB, 2007-2010).

Ele deve se juntar ainda nesta semana à equipe de transição de governos. Novos nomes devem ser anunciados por Zucco nesta quinta-feira (26) . O primeiro escalão da próxima gestão tem 13 secretários conhecidos, enquanto os titulares de cinco pastas seguem indefinidos . (Veja relação abaixo)

Engenheiro civil, empresário e conselheiro de administração pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Governança Corporativa (IBGC), Andrade é pós-graduado em Gestão Empresarial, com formação executiva internacional pelo IESE, da Universidade de Navarra, na Espanha.

Foi secretário de Infraestrutura do Rio Grande do Sul durante o governo Yeda Crusius (PSDB, 2007-2011), presidente do Fórum Nacional dos Secretários de Energia e chefe da área de planejamento da Trensurb, onde foi responsável pela gestão dos recursos do Banco Mundial (BIRD) destinados à construção do trem.

Também atuou como diretor de novos negócios de uma empresa de porte nacional e, como empresário, gerenciou o planejamento e a fiscalização de obras como a Arena do Grêmio, a Usina Termelétrica de Candiota – Fase C, a sede corporativa da Fecomércio-RS, o Centro de Inovação e Tecnologia da Ambev, no Rio de Janeiro, e o Centro Cultural CEEE Erico Verissimo.

articles.title: Embraer: EUA propõem tarifa de 10% sobre aviões brasileiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Fabricante com sede em São José dos Campos defende manutenção da tarifa zero para o setor aeroespacial; empresa afirma ter US$ 3,5 bilhões em ativos e mais de 2,5 mil funcionários nos Estados Unidos.
articles.summary: A Embraer analisa a proposta dos EUA de aplicar tarifa de 10% sobre aviões brasileiros e defende a isenção para proteger seus US$ 3,5 bilhões em ativos no país.
articles.body:
Embraer. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A Embraer , fabricante de aeronaves com sede em São José dos Campos , no interior de São Paulo, informou que está analisando o relatório publicado pelo governo dos Estados Unidos nesta quarta-feira (25), que considera a possibilidade de aplicar uma tarifa adicional de 10% sobre a importação de aviões brasileiros.

Atualmente, os produtos da Embraer exportados para os Estados Unidos não são taxados. A proposta do governo americano prevê retirar as aeronaves brasileiras prontas da lista de exceções ao tarifaço e estabelecer uma nova cobrança.

Em nota, a empresa afirmou que defende a manutenção do regime de tarifa zero para a indústria aeroespacial global, em vigor desde a década de 1980.

A fabricante também destacou sua presença no mercado americano. Segundo a Embraer, a companhia investe nos Estados Unidos há mais de 45 anos, onde mantém instalações industriais, US$ 3,5 bilhões em ativos e mais de 2,5 mil funcionários.

A empresa afirma ainda que esses investimentos geram benefícios econômicos para os dois países e cita um superávit comercial de US$ 8 bilhões para a economia americana nos próximos cinco anos.

A mudança foi apresentada pelo Escritório do Representante Comercial dos Estados Unidos (USTR, na sigla em inglês), após uma investigação comercial conduzida com base na Seção 301 da Lei de Comércio Americana.

Atualmente, as aeronaves brasileiras estão entre os produtos isentos da tarifa adicional de 25% aplicada à parte das mercadorias brasileiras.

A proposta ainda não entrou em vigor. O governo americano abriu uma consulta pública sobre as mudanças. A audiência está prevista para 14 de janeiro de 2027, e o prazo para envio de comentários por escrito termina em 30 de dezembro de 2026.

Ainda não há uma data definida para eventual início da cobrança.

articles.title: Feminicídio em SC: Estado lança pacto para fortalecer proteção | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Marco Zero' do Ministério Público reúne órgãos públicos, prefeituras e empresários para fortalecer rede de proteção e prevenir mortes de mulheres.
articles.summary: O pacto Marco Zero contra o feminicídio em SC integra órgãos públicos e empresas para acolher vítimas e oferecer autonomia financeira em 32 novos núcleos de apoio.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Santa Catarina lançou, nesta quarta-feira (25), um pacto para fortalecer a rede de proteção às mulheres e ampliar o combate à violência de gênero.

Batizada de "Marco Zero de Enfrentamento ao Feminicídio: Do Mapa à Proteção", a iniciativa reúne órgãos públicos, prefeituras e entidades empresariais para prevenir agressões e evitar mortes. O projeto prevê a criação de núcleos de apoio para vítimas de crimes graves e ações para fortalecer a autonomia financeira das mulheres (veja mais abaixo).

O lançamento ocorreu em Florianópolis , no Dia Internacional pela Eliminação da Violência Contra as Mulheres.

A mobilização ocorre em um momento de alta nos crimes de gênero: neste ano, 51 feminicídios foram registrados no estado até esta quarta-feira , segundo o Ministério Público de Santa Catarina (MPSC), idealizador do projeto.

O principal motivador do pacto é um dado do Mapa do Feminicídio de Santa Catarina , elaborado pelo MPSC: entre 2020 e 2024, 73% das vítimas de feminicídio no estado não tinham medida protetiva de urgência.

O objetivo do Marco Zero é ampliar a identificação de situações de risco, fortalecendo o atendimento e a proteção às vítimas antes que a violência se torne letal.

"As nossas filhas e netas não podem esperar. Mulheres continuam morrendo simplesmente por serem mulheres", afirmou a procuradora-geral de Justiça do MPSC, Vanessa Wendhausen Cavallazzi, durante a assinatura do pacto.

Além do Ministério Público, participam da iniciativa as secretarias estaduais da Saúde e da Assistência Social, Mulher e Família, a Federação de Consórcios, Associações de Municípios e Municípios de Santa Catarina (Fecam), prefeituras e a Federação das Associações Empresariais de Santa Catarina (Facisc).

Projeto prevê integração entre diferentes setores

O plano prevê a atuação conjunta de serviços de saúde, assistência social, segurança pública e outros setores da rede de atendimento. O foco é capacitar profissionais para reconhecer sinais de agressão, acolher as vítimas e encaminhá-las aos serviços adequados.

Durante o evento, o secretário de Estado da Saúde, Diogo Demarchi Silva, destacou a importância do diagnóstico precoce.

"Qualificar não é para preencher um papel. É fazer com que esse trabalhador possa identificar sinais, saber escutar esse relato e saber para onde encaminhar as demandas daquela mulher, de maneira intersetorial", afirmou Silva.

Durante o lançamento, o governo anunciou a ampliação dos Núcleos de Enfrentamento às Violências e Apoio às Vítimas (Neavits). Os espaços oferecem suporte a vítimas de crimes graves, com foco em grupos sociais vulneráveis.

Segundo a coordenadora-geral dos núcleos, a promotora de Justiça Chimelly Marcon, o estado passa a contar com 32 estruturas ativas a partir desta quarta-feira.

O evento também ofereceu treinamento para as equipes dos núcleos, com o objetivo de fortalecer o atendimento especializado em todas as regiões catarinenses.

Autonomia financeira também faz parte da iniciativa

Outro ponto de destaque é a autonomia financeira para ajudar as mulheres a romper o ciclo de violência. O Serviço Brasileiro de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas (Sebrae) em Santa Catarina estuda uma parceria para oferecer capacitação e incentivo ao empreendedorismo para as vítimas.

A gestora de projetos da entidade, Alessandra Pinheiro, destacou que a dependência financeira é uma das principais barreiras para o fim de relações abusivas. A proposta é conectar as vítimas a projetos como o "Sebrae Delas", focado na geração de renda.

O presidente da Facisc, Elson Otto, ressaltou o papel do setor produtivo na criação de oportunidades de trabalho para que essas mulheres reconstruam suas vidas.

"Nós queremos que, num futuro próximo, zero seja o nosso número de feminicídios no Estado", reforçou Chimelly.

articles.title: Army detonates cache of lead explosives, with toxic plume possible across Iowa
articles.summary: The Army detonated a stockpile of unstable lead azide explosives in Iowa on Wednesday morning. A toxic dust plume could travel for miles.
articles.body: The Army detonated a stockpile of unstable lead azide explosives in southeast Iowa on Wednesday in a blast that was expected to spread lead dust for miles. The detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown was intended to eliminate 68 drums of deteriorating, toxic lead azide — about 9,700 pounds. The Army said the material had become “recrystallized” inside and outside the drums, putting it at risk of a spontaneous explosion and making it unsafe to move. NBC affiliate KWQC of Iowa filmed the detonation from a location in Danville, about 4 miles north of the plant. Just after 9 a.m. local time, the camera feed captured two blasts of gray and white smoke that appeared to dissipate after about 30 seconds. Reporter Cyle Dickens said he felt a “percussion” from the explosion and a shock wave that traveled across a farm field toward him. Linda Ross, who lives about a mile southwest of the site, said she felt “very little shaking” in the moments after the blast. “Two short boom boom sounds. Dog started barking. That’s about it,” she said. Still, Ross added, it was “unnerving.” “We will stay inside today,” she said. A host of state and federal leaders sought to offer the public assurances after the blast, including President Donald Trump and Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds. However, independent experts have said it will take some time to determine how much lead was deposited and what the risks to nearby communities could be. Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, the commanding general of the U.S. Army Sustainment Command that led the U.S. Army-controlled detonation, said it had exceeded his expectations. “I believe absolutely that we reduced as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown,” Shirley said in a video message broadcast by the Army. “As we saw in the immediate aftermath through overhead coverage, all of the lead azide barrels were definitively removed. There was no secondary explosions. ... There was no infrastructure damage in or around our installation.” Shirley attributed the visible clouds that emanated from the blast site to the foam solution the Army sprayed there. Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, said in the video that military personnel had successfully driven the explosion “into the ground,” minimizing pollution. The Environmental Protection Agency, which approved the Army’s permit to detonate, said air quality monitors were reporting “ZERO detection of airborne lead throughout the region.” However, previous modeling suggested it would take several hours for the dust plume to disperse. Multiple experts agreed that it’s too early to make conclusions about lead pollution levels. Andrew Whelton, a professor of civil, environmental and ecological engineering at Purdue University in Indiana, said that although the EPA’s real-time air monitoring data suggests some potentially promising results, “physical analysis” of samples is necessary. “Multiple lines of evidence are needed,” he said. Still, Whelton said that in video footage, the blast appeared smaller than what he had expected, given the Army’s descriptions ahead of time. “It’s possible that if there is a lead release, it is more contained to the detonation site than it could have been,” he said. Before the explosion, the Army had called for evacuations in Middletown and a 5-mile zone to the southwest of the ammunition plant. Soldiers went door to door Tuesday afternoon to notify residents that they should evacuate. The Federal Emergency Management Agency is providing short-term hotel lodging to those in the evacuation zone through Friday. Based on Wednesday’s expected weather conditions, Army projections indicated the cloud of lead dust could travel some 100 miles southwest and cross into northeastern Missouri. The plan prompted widespread fear and anger among local residents in the days before the detonation, with many saying they did not receive enough warning. People in the potential path of the plume scrambled to change Thanksgiving plans, tape windows, cover gardens, buy cleaning supplies and, in some places, get their families out of town. Jill Holler, who has a family farm about 20 miles west of Middletown, said she spent Sunday night rushing to take soil samples for future comparisons of lead concentrations. “I was down in the dark getting the soil samples, and it’s just frustrating,” she said. Lead is a potent neurotoxin and no amount of exposure is safe. It poses the biggest health threat to children. Exposure is associated with learning disabilities, reproductive health problems, mental health issues and increased risk of hearing loss, among other effects. Once deposited on surfaces or in soil, lead particles can remain there forever unless physically removed. Army officials have maintained that it was safer to detonate the chemicals in a controlled manner, with mitigation measures in place, than risk a surprise blast. Before the detonation, they described a range of mitigation strategies intended to keep as much lead dust as possible within the ammunition plant. That included two stories of “HESCO” barriers — modular, collapsible structures filled with sand — built around the detonation site and a plan to spray water during the explosion to catch small particles. Officials also said aqueous foam blocks, gel blocks and two “water walls” made of four 16,000-gallon water tanks each would help absorb the blast. In a statement after the detonation on Wednesday, Iowa Governor-elect Rob Sand said that although more testing needs to be done, federal officials had told him everything had gone well. Still, he added, “the lead-up to the detonation should never have been so chaotic and unclear.” According to emergency permitting documents submitted to the EPA, the Army expected the blast to leave a crater about 38 feet wide and 5 feet deep. The Army said in a release Tuesday that after the detonation, environmental monitoring teams would follow the plume’s path “to collect soil, surface-water, and surface-wipe samples to verify lead levels.” If any residential properties are found to exceed a certain threshold of lead contamination — 200 parts per million — the Army said, “remediation teams will remove affected soil, clean surfaces, and restore the property at complete government expense.” It offered few specifics, however, about how or when such testing would be conducted — or the process or timeline for any government-led remediation work. Whelton said that even the Army’s emergency permit did not describe those plans in detail. “Based on the document I reviewed, there is no plan for applying an evidence-based approach to determine if people’s homes, schools, and businesses are safe after the detonation,” he said on Tuesday. Peter Thorne, a pulmonary toxicologist and environmental health specialist with the University of Iowa’s College of Public Health, said that scientists planned to conduct independent monitoring of the plume. “We have monitoring equipment out there that’s going to tell us the extent of lead that’s became airborne and moved with the wind,” he said Tuesday. “Our models will be able to tell us how much lead is depositing on soil and on playground equipment and so forth. And from that, we can make some estimates of what the degree of danger is associated with this exposure.” The nation’s stockpile of lead azide — once used to make bomb triggers but mostly phased out of the process about 15 years ago — was moved to the ammunition plant in 2009, officials have said. Cekada said Tuesday that the chemicals were known even at that time to pose a problem. Thorne questioned how these explosives were allowed to become so dangerous over so many years. “It should have been dealt with in the past, and now it’s become a crisis,” he said.

articles.title: DANNY DANON: From Auschwitz to the UN, Israel must never retreat
articles.summary: Dozens of United Nations ambassadors walked through Auschwitz as antisemitism surges, and Israel's envoy says the next secretary-general must act.
articles.body: Earlier this month, at a time when antisemitism is surging around the world, I walked with dozens of United Nations ambassadors through the haunted gates of Auschwitz. No matter how many times I return to that hallowed ground, the experience never becomes easier. Each visit reminds me of the devastating cost of antisemitism and the catastrophic consequences of a world that remains silent in the face of hatred. This diplomatic mission came at a critical moment. The race to elect the next U.N. secretary-general is advancing quickly. Whoever assumes this position must confront the institutional antisemitism that has taken root within the U.N. AMBASSADOR JEFF BARTOS: UN MUST ABANDON ANTI-AMERICAN, ANTI-WESTERN LEGACY OF DURBAN CONFERENCE This institutional antisemitism is prevalent throughout the U.N. Headquarters. We hear it from U.N. officials, read it in U.N. reports and even encounter it in the secretary-general’s own rhetoric. An institution founded in the aftermath of the Holocaust can't claim to fight antisemitism while providing a platform for the demonization of Israel. As representatives of the Jewish state, we have a responsibility to address this issue. But we cannot do it alone. We must leverage our diplomatic relationships to build coalitions with other nations and ensure that combating antisemitism becomes a collective international priority. That is why, in September, we established a task force of U.N. member states to combat antisemitism within the organization and around the world. At our inaugural meeting, we focused on translating declarations against Jew hatred into concrete action. The next secretary-general must build on these efforts, not allow them to fade into another round of empty promises. Our mission to Poland was a natural extension of that work. We must ensure that the memory of the Holocaust remains permanently etched in the international community’s consciousness. Never again means nothing if the world forgets what happened before. THE ANTISEMITISM HORSESHOE IS PLAYING OUT IN REAL TIME — FROM NEW YORK TO PARIS AND BEYOND For many of the ambassadors accompanying me, this was their first encounter with the remnants of the Holocaust. They had studied it, heard about it and read about it. But nothing compares to standing on the very ground where the Nazis committed their atrocities. Witnessing history is only the beginning. My colleagues must return to their countries determined to confront antisemitism not just at the U.N., but in their own countries as well. Around the world, 2025 was the deadliest year for antisemitic violence in three decades, with more than twenty people killed in at least four attacks. In the United States, FBI data shows that antisemitism remains the most prevalent form of religiously motivated hate crime. Although Jews account for less than 3% of the population, they were targeted in 63% of religiously motivated hate crimes in 2025. And this wave of hatred has not yet broken. Earlier this month, on the eve of Kristallnacht, an anti-Israel bike rally targeted Jewish and Israeli-owned restaurants in Philadelphia, accusing them of supporting "genocide." The rhetoric echoed familiar antisemitic patterns of prewar Europe: demonize Jews, assign collective guilt and turn hatred into a campaign of intimidation. Being in Poland allowed me to confront these realities alongside my colleagues against the backdrop of history. But the most important part of this mission came when I brought the delegation to Israel. SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER There, I showed my colleagues the beauty of our country, the strength of our people and the challenges we continue to face. They visited the sites of the Oct. 7 massacre and received informative briefings on the realities Israel confronts. The visit underscored why a strong, independent Jewish state is indispensable. Israel is not merely a refuge from antisemitism. It is the eternal homeland of the Jewish people; a country capable of defending its people, preserving its history and shaping its own future. At a time when many question whether Israel should continue engaging with the U.N., this mission reinforces exactly why we must. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Despite the relentless hostility Israel faces within the organization, we cannot afford to abandon the battlefield. We must remain, confront the lies, challenge the bias and find creative ways to achieve meaningful diplomatic victories. Fighting antisemitism requires education, firsthand encounters with history and conversations that challenge entrenched misconceptions about Israel and the Jewish people. Most importantly, fighting antisemitism requires leadership. The next secretary-general will inherit an institution facing a profound credibility crisis. Combating antisemitism must be more than another campaign promise. It must become a defining test of leadership for every candidate. The diplomats who joined this mission learned a powerful lesson that no meeting or lecture could convey: we must confront hatred before it becomes catastrophe. Speeches alone are not sufficient to combat antisemitism. It requires concrete action, institutional accountability and a willingness to confront those who spread hatred. We will take that lesson back to the United Nations. We will continue building coalitions, challenging antisemitism and demanding that the institution live up to the principles on which it was founded. We intend to make sure that choice cannot be ignored.

articles.title: Saharanpur showdown: Why Akhilesh's 1st candidate list in UP has rattled Congress MP Imran Masood
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood is breathing fire at the Samajwadi Party after Akhilesh Yadav's first candidate list for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood is breathing fire at the Samajwadi Party after Akhilesh Yadav's first candidate list for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The list includes two constituencies that the Congress leader considers his political turf. The SP's decision to renominate sitting MLAs from Behat and Saharanpur, both seats sought by Congress in alliance negotiations, has turned a seat-sharing disagreement into a personal and political confrontation.Released on Tuesday night, hours after another round of seat-sharing talks between the two parties in Delhi, the five-name list features four Muslim candidates from western Uttar Pradesh and an OBC nominee from Bundelkhand. The four Muslim candidates are sitting MLAs Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha. Jyoti Lodhi has been named from Lalitpur.The move has particularly rattled Masood, who represents Saharanpur in the Lok Sabha and is the Congress's Uttar Pradesh working president. Having won the Saharanpur parliamentary seat in 2024, Masood sees the two qssembly constituencies as important to Congress's claim to political space in the region. His sharp response has raised a pointed question: does the SP want to take on the BJP or its INDIA bloc ally?The Saharanpur warThe SP renominated four sitting legislators: Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha. The fifth candidate, Jyoti Lodhi, has been named from Lalitpur.All four Muslim candidates are from western UP, where the SP is keen to retain its traditional support base and expand its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) coalition.But Behat and Saharanpur make the list particularly sensitive for Masood.The Congress MP won the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat in 2024 with 5,47,967 votes, defeating the BJP's Raghav Lakhanpal by 64,542 votes. He secured 44.57% of the vote, against the BJP candidate's 39.32%.His performance was particularly strong in the two assembly segments now at the centre of the dispute. Masood led by 44,626 votes in Saharanpur and 38,229 in Behat in the parliamentary election. Both, however, had elected SP MLAs in 2022.Umar Ali Khan won Behat with 1,34,513 votes, defeating the BJP's Naresh Saini by 37,880 votes. Ashu Malik secured Saharanpur with 1,07,007 votes, defeating the BJP's Jagpal Singh by 30,745 votes.The contrast is the main disagreement point between the allies. Congress is banking on the 2024 Lok Sabha mandate, while the SP is relying on its assembly-level victories and sitting legislators.For Akhilesh, the two seats are established SP territory. However, for Masood, they are part of the space where Congress can consolidate after his parliamentary victory.Masood and Malik were involved in a public exchange during a district development coordination and monitoring committee meeting earlier this year. After the SP announcement, Malik said he was under "no fear or pressure" and would contest the election strongly.Masood's nephew Hamza Masood was more combative. He asserted that Congress would contest all seven assembly seats in Saharanpur district, adding that his uncle's support was crucial in the region."BJP ko Saharanpur se Imran Masood hi hara sakte hain," he said.The Akhilesh-Masood equationThe latest confrontation is another turn in a political relationship that has changed parties, positions and equations more than once.Imran Masood left Congress and joined the SP in January 2022, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. But the association lasted barely nine months. After the SP did not give him or his associates a ticket, Masood quit the party in October 2022 and joined the BSP.Mayawati appointed him coordinator of the BSP's western Uttar Pradesh unit, with additional responsibility for working among Muslims in Uttarakhand. That stint, too, ended abruptly. In August 2023, the BSP expelled him, accusing him of indiscipline and anti-party activities. Masood returned to Congress in October that year.The return proved electorally significant. In 2024, Congress fielded him from Saharanpur as part of the INDIA bloc arrangement, with SP support. He defeated the BJP, giving Congress a prominent Muslim face in western UP.But the parliamentary victory did not necessarily settle the question of who would control the political space in the region.The unease has been building for months. Congress's decision to appoint Masood as Uttar Pradesh working president in October was viewed by some SP leaders as an attempt to strengthen its bargaining position in seat-sharing negotiations. The Indian Express reported that sections of the SP were uncomfortable with Masood's public criticism of Akhilesh and his demands for an early alliance decision.In August, another development added to the strain. Imran Masood's son-in-law, Shayan Masood, joined the SP, citing ideological differences with his father-in-law. Shayan subsequently criticised Masood for targeting Akhilesh instead of the BJP.The candidate announcement has now brought the personal and political tensions into the open."When you make such an announcement against me, I don't understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress, or the BJP," Masood said, questioning the SP's seriousness about the alliance.He also rejected the idea that Congress was seeking charity from the SP. "We are not beggars," he said, objecting to the party's unilateral announcement of candidates while negotiations were still underway.Elder brothers or stepbrothers?The public sparring quickly drew reactions from both camps, with some leaders attempting damage control and others adding fuel to the fire.SP leader ST Hasan urged restraint, describing the two parties as elder and younger brothers."We are like elder and younger brothers. We should not talk like two stepbrothers fighting over division of property," he said.SP MP SP Singh Patel, however, was less conciliatory. He dismissed Congress's electoral strength in Uttar Pradesh and said the party would only be able to win by relying on the SP."The Congress should simply accept whatever number of seats they are allocated in the alliance," he said.Masood hit back, invoking Rahul Gandhi's role in Patel's political rise. He argued that Patel was an MP because of the political impact Rahul Gandhi had created after 2019.The exchange has exposed a fundamental disagreement over the alliance's power structure. Congress wants its improved Lok Sabha performance recognised; the SP believes its much larger Assembly-level organisation should determine the terms.The voter mathStrip away the personal exchanges and the five-candidate announcement points to a larger contest over political representation in western Uttar Pradesh.The region has considerable electoral significance for both parties. Saharanpur district, according to Census 2011 data, had a Muslim population of 41.9% and a Scheduled Caste population of 22.1%. These are district-wide population figures, not constituency-level voter shares, but they underline the social context in which the two parties are positioning themselves.For the SP, the PDA formula is an attempt to bring backward classes, Dalits and minorities into a broader electoral coalition. Renominating four Muslim sitting MLAs in its first list reinforces the party's commitment to that strategy.Congress, meanwhile, sees its 2024 performance as an opportunity to rebuild its own Muslim-Dalit political base, particularly in western UP. Masood's Saharanpur victory gave the party a prominent regional leader around whom it can attempt to build that presence.The competition is not limited to the two INDIA bloc partners either. The Samajik Parivartan Morcha, a new alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram), is another political formation seeking space among Muslim and Dalit voters.The BSP, too, remains part of the wider political equation, even as its organisational position has changed since the 2022 election.The SP has released a list of five, but the questions they have raised go well beyond Behat and Saharanpur. Who speaks for western UP's Muslim voters? How much space will Congress get within Akhilesh Yadav's PDA framework? And can two allies compete for the same electoral ground without undermining the alliance they are trying to build?For now, the SP has made its choices clear. Whether Congress accepts them, and whether the two parties can turn this confrontation into a workable seat-sharing arrangement, remains the bigger test.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Call to backdate law change to killer parents rights
articles.summary: Jade's Law will automatically suspend parental rights after a domestic murder from December.
articles.body:
Survivors and campaigners are in Westminster urging MPs to backdate Jade's Law, new legislation coming into force in December that automatically suspends parental rights after a domestic murder.

Jade's Law was campaigned for by the family of Jade Ward , who was 27 when she was murdered by ex-partner Russell Marsh in Flintshire, Wales, in 2021.

Currently, the rules won't apply to cases before the legislation comes into force in December - but an Oxfordshire charity is calling for that to be changed.

Jake Richards, the Minister for Sentencing, Human Rights and Technology, said the new law would "help ensure children's safety and welfare come first".

Jade's Law follows a campaign by the parents of Jade Ward, after Marsh asked for pictures and school reports from prison following his conviction.

The legislation, which means parents who kill someone they have children with will have parental rights suspended on sentencing, will come into force in England and Wales on 18 December.

The charity Children Heard and Seen, which is based in Cumnor, supports children with a parent in prison, and is calling for the law to be introduced retrospectively.

Sarah Burrows, founder of the charity, said the new law was "obviously going to be really good", but "unfortunately won't affect" the families Children Heard and Seen already works with.

"They are still controlled and they have to go through the family courts to fight to get these restrictions partially lifted," Burrows said.

She said there was a recent example of a grandmother who had wanted to take children on holiday following the end of their father's trial so they could "start grieving".

"They then couldn't go on holiday because the father, who had killed their daughter, the children's mother, wasn't allowing it."

"It's things like that that I don't think people would think actually does happen."

Junior minister Richards agreed that "children's safety must always come first".

He said Jade's Law would "automatically restrict the exercise of parental responsibility of parents who murder their child's other parent... limiting the decisions they can make about their child's life".

"We'll also no longer require courts to presume that each parent should be involved in a child's life, while remaining clear that involvement should continue where it is safe and in the child's best interests," he said.

"Alongside our national rollout of Child Focused Courts, these reforms will help ensure children's safety and welfare come first."

articles.title: Amnesty seeks independent probe into possible war crimes in Tigray
articles.summary: Amnesty International on Tuesday called for an investigation into possible war crimes after Ethiopian forces and an allied militia allegedly shelled
articles.body: Amnesty International on Tuesday called for an investigation into possible war crimes after Ethiopian forces and an allied militia allegedly shelled civilian neighbourhoods in the Tigray region. The warning comes amid renewed fighting and growing concerns among residents living near the Eritrean border about the possibility of another war.According to news agency AP, the human rights organisation said it had independently verified the deaths of 14 civilians in four artillery attacks on the city of Alamata between September 26 and 28. The attacks took place as Ethiopian forces and the allied Tigray peace forces advanced towards the city.Amnesty also accused forces allied with the Tigray people's liberation front (TPLF) of putting civilians at risk by setting up military positions in residential neighbourhoods and schools. The TPLF rejected the allegations in a written response to the organisation.The findings come amid escalating tensions in Tigray and fears that the renewed conflict could lead to a wider confrontation between Ethiopia and neighbouring Eritrea.Amnesty said its investigation involved interviews with local residents, survivors and medical workers. It also examined videos, photographs and satellite images to verify the reported attacks.The Ethiopian government and military had not responded to the report. Amnesty said neither the military nor the allied militia had replied to its questions before publication.Residents near Eritrean border fear another warMeanwhile, residents in border areas of Tigray are preparing for the possibility of renewed conflict.Berhe Sibagadis, a 41-year-old father of four from Alitena in Tigray's Irob district, said he was planning to move his family away from the Eritrean border to a safer location in central Tigray."I have to save my family, therefore I have to move to the centre of Tigray," he told the Associated Press over the phone.Sibagadis claimed that Eritrean forces were occupying part of his local administrative area inside Ethiopian territory. He also recalled abuses allegedly committed by Eritrean troops during the 2020-2022 war."Eritrean forces committed a crime against our community during the 2020 war, so why should we stay here?" he said.The two-year conflict in Tigray resulted in an estimated 500,000 civilian deaths due to violence, famine and the breakdown of healthcare services, according to researchers at Belgium's Ghent University.Human rights organisations and United Nations experts had accused Eritrean troops of committing abuses during the war. However, Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki dismissed the allegations as "a fantasy" in 2023.Another resident of Irob, Hagos Niguse, said Eritrean soldiers were present in his area within Ethiopian territory. He claimed to have seen troops moving tanks and heavy weapons towards the border and constructing military fortifications.In Rama, another resident, Yonas Desta, reported military movements and drones flying overhead."Both countries are preparing for war and we cannot sleep when we think what could happen tomorrow," he said.Hagos and Yonas also claimed that TPLF fighters were positioned alongside Eritrean forces. During the 2020-2022 conflict, Eritrean troops had fought alongside the Ethiopian military against Tigrayan forces.Former allies face growing military tensionsThe conflict monitoring organisation armed conflict location & event data (ACLED) reported that Ethiopian forces carried out drone strikes on suspected Eritrean positions near Badme on November 12. The attacks were followed by Eritrean artillery fire and direct clashes.ACLED's senior analyst for East Africa, Jalale Getachew Birru, warned that the possibility of a major military confrontation along the Badme front had increased."The risk of a full-scale military confrontation along the Badme front is now high," he said in comments sent by email on November 17.According to ACLED, Eritrean troops returned to Badme around November 15 after withdrawing in October. They reportedly deployed reinforcements as Ethiopian forces gathered nearby.Badme was a major flashpoint during the 1998-2000 border war between Ethiopia and Eritrea, which killed around 70,000 people, according to the UN peacekeeping mission established after the conflict.Relations between the two countries improved following a 2018 peace agreement. The rapprochement also helped Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed win the 2019 Nobel peace prize.However, ties have deteriorated in recent years. Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of supporting Tigrayan rebels, an allegation that Asmara denies. Tensions have also increased over Abiy's demand for access to Eritrea's red sea coastline.Fighting resumed in September despite a November 2022 agreement that had brought an end to the two-year conflict in Tigray.Rahel Kidane, a 35-year-old shopkeeper from Sheraro, said she had spent more than two years living with relatives in Axum after fleeing the earlier war. She returned to her hometown following the peace agreement.However, renewed fighting has once again left her worried about being forced to leave her home."I live in fear of being displaced again," she told the AP over the phone. articles.title: Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
articles.summary: Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.
articles.body:
Solomon Islands and Australia have signed a sweeping treaty affirming that the small Pacific country will allow no foreign military bases on its territory.

The deal, signed on Wednesday, is seen as a blow to the regional ambitions of China, which had been moving closer to the Solomon Islands for years.

“Solomon Islands has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are gone,” Prime Minister Matthew Wale told journalists alongside his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese.

The treaty establishes Australia as the island nation’s “primary security partner” and will see Canberra provide 740 million Australian dollars ($490m) over the next 10 years to fund free education and other programmes in Solomon Islands. Solomon Islands has a gross domestic product (GDP) of $1.75bn, according to the World Bank.

In exchange, Solomon Islands will allow no foreign military or security bases on its soil, and the country’s “sensitive” infrastructure will “remain free from militarisation, foreign interference and unauthorised access”.

That includes ports, airports, energy and telecommunications, as well as road and bridge construction – areas China has dominated in the islands through its Belt and Road Initiative. The deal will not apply retroactively.

Solomon Islands will also have to consult Australia before making deals involving its critical infrastructure or security cooperation unless it is with members of the Pacific Islands Forum regional bloc, Albanese said.

Since being elected in May, Wale has upended Solomon Islands’ diplomatic moves towards China and realigned with Australia and the United States.

Asked about reports he had ended a secretive security pact with Beijing, Wale told journalists that discussions with China were “ongoing”.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not confirm whether the deal had been scrapped, but warned that the new agreement with Australia “should not target any third party”.

This is the latest in a string of similar deals Australia has struck with Pacific states, including Papua New Guinea , Vanuatu and Fiji .

articles.title: Visa scam: Indian-origin kingpin Chandrakant Patel sentenced to 10 years in prison; will be deported after jail sentence
articles.summary: A Louisiana businessman who orchestrated a visa fraud scheme involving fabricated armed robbery reports has been sentenced to 10 years in federal prison,
articles.body: A Louisiana businessman who orchestrated a visa fraud scheme involving fabricated armed robbery reports has been sentenced to 10 years in federal prison, while four former law enforcement officials who helped him carry out the operation have each received five-year prison terms. The US Citizenship and Immigration Services announced the sentencing of Chandrakant “Lala” Patel, 40, of Oakdale, Louisiana, who was convicted of conspiracy to commit visa fraud and conducting financial transactions involving proceeds from unlawful activity. Patel will be removed from the United States after completing his prison sentence, authorities said.The four co-conspirators were identified as Tebo Onishea, 39, former police chief of Glenmora; Chad Doyle, 56, former police chief of Oakdale; Michael Slaney, 65, former Ward 5 marshal in Oakdale; and Glynn Dixon, 63, former police chief of Forest Hill. All four were sentenced to 60 months in federal prison for conspiracy to commit visa fraud. Doyle, Slaney and Dixon were also ordered to pay $30,000 fines each, followed by two years of supervised release.According to court documents, the conspiracy operated between November 2020 and July 2025. Patel recruited foreign nationals seeking legal status in the US and collected thousands of dollars from them in exchange for falsely identifying them as victims of armed robberies that had never occurred.He then paid the four law enforcement officials to prepare fabricated police reports and certify immigration documents that were used to support fraudulent U visa applications. The former officials exploited their positions in local law enforcement to authenticate the false reports, giving the fabricated incidents the appearance of legitimate criminal investigations.How the U visa fraud scheme workedThe operation targeted the U nonimmigrant visa program that provides immigration protection to certain victims of qualifying crimes who assist law enforcement authorities in investigating or prosecuting criminal activity. The program was created to encourage noncitizens who are victims of crimes to cooperate with police without fearing that their immigration status would prevent them from coming forward.To qualify, applicants must meet specific requirements, including being victims of qualifying criminal activity and possessing information about the crime. They also generally need a certification from an authorized law enforcement agency confirming their victimisation and cooperation.Patel exploited this requirement by arranging for foreign nationals to be named as victims in fictional armed robbery cases. The police officials then prepared reports documenting the non-existent crimes and certified the immigration paperwork supporting the applications.Court records also revealed that the conspirators transmitted fraudulent documents through the US Postal Service and other interstate carriers to advance the operation.The investigation revealed that Patel had attempted to bribe an agent of the Rapides Parish Sheriff's Office with $5,000 in February 2025 to obtain another fabricated police report.Five defendants pleaded guiltyThe five defendants, including Patel, were originally indicted in July 2025. They pleaded guilty to their respective charges between May and June 2026. Patel pleaded guilty on May 28, 2026, to conspiracy to commit visa fraud and engaging in monetary transactions involving property derived from unlawful activity.Onishea pleaded guilty on May 28, while Doyle entered his guilty plea on May 20. Slaney pleaded guilty on May 12, and Dixon pleaded guilty on June 30.US District Judge Jerry Edwards Jr handed down Patel's 120-month sentence on November 9, 2026. Dixon was sentenced to five years on the same day. The other three officials had received their sentences earlier. articles.title: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war, new estimate suggests
articles.summary: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine, according to a new projection based on leaked official data, an estimate that sheds new light on the staggering cost of President Vladimir Putin’s war.
articles.body: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine, according to a new projection based on leaked official data, an estimate that sheds new light on the staggering cost of President Vladimir Putin’s war. The grim assessment comes more than 4½ years after the Kremlin’s invasion of its neighbor, an all-out war that has consumed Russian society. The death toll has been mounting with each painstaking ground assault, with no end to the conflict in sight despite pressure from President Donald Trump for Kyiv to make a deal. The leak from Russia’s state statistics agency, Rosstat — released by Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers earlier this month — reveals that at least 490,000 Russian soldiers had been killed in Ukraine based on registered deaths as of the end of September. That’s according to breakdowns by a range of independent media, including the BBC and others, that were published this week. But one exiled Russian media outlet, Meduza, also used the leaked mortality data to project the total number of military deaths, including those that have not yet been recorded. Meduza estimates that number to be 720,000. NBC News did not have access to the leaked data and could not authenticate it or independently confirm these numbers. Neither Moscow nor Kyiv provide regular updates on their battlefield losses. Mediazona, along with the BBC Russian Service and a team of volunteers, has been compiling a separate named list of Russian war dead using open-source data for years, given the difficulty of gauging the true impact of the war on Russian society. In its analysis, Mediazona said it arrived at the 490,000 war dead number from the 29.7 million records it obtained from the hackers that covered nearly all death registrations in Russia from early 2021 through September this year, based mainly on records with an “explicit military cause of death” and court rulings declaring people dead. The leaked data was cross-checked against Mediazona’s own named list and matched 95% of the records, as well as the publicly accessible national Probate Registry, a database of inheritance cases, and Rosstat’s own official mortality statistics, the outlet said. Mediazona said it also checked against possible data tempering and fake military death injections by cross-referencing a unique vital record number that every death registration carries, and court rulings, which often cite death record numbers. “We are confident that this data is genuine,” the outlet said, adding that fabricating a dataset of this scale from scratch would be “impossible” especially as it checks out against official registries. The hackers shared leaked data with a number of other exiled Russian media outlets and the BBC, who all arrived at a figure close to the 490,000 reported by Mediazona. A similar estimate of half a million Russian troops killed was also shared by a senior British defense official in September. Before the new analysis of the data in the Rosstat leak, the verified named list of Russia’s war dead compiled by Mediazona and the BBC stood at just over 289,000. It was based on obituaries, local news and official registries, and was the only publicly available database containing the fallen soldiers’ names. The Russian Defense Ministry has not officially updated its death toll in Ukraine since the early months of the war, when then-Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu said it stood at nearly 6,000. Mediazona warned that due to a considerable lag in military death registrations, Rosstat may not yet have finished capturing deaths from 2025. “That means the leaked records through late September — however authentic and reliable they are — still fall short of the true death toll,” it said. It was this that prompted Meduza to try and calculate an estimate of total Russian losses to date — 720,000 people, a figure that includes deaths it predicts will be registered later. “Since 2024, the share of late registrations has grown dramatically, and it continues to rise,” the outlet said in its own analysis, adding that the 2026 data is extremely incomplete for both missing service members and other military deaths. It said it used epidemiology and tools like the “chain-ladder method” from actuarial science, which uses mathematics to help measure the probability and risk of future events, to arrive at the projected estimate. These methods allowed Meduza to calculate the number of military deaths that it estimates have happened but haven’t yet shown up in the data, the outlet said. “Today, it’s simply impossible to leave this category out of an overall estimate of the dead,” it added. The Kremlin dismissed the analysis Wednesday. “The only department authorized to officially release data on casualties is the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation,” spokesman Dmitry Peskov told NBC News during a call with reporters, when asked if the Kremlin was aware of the 700,000 projected estimate by Meduza. “I suggest disregarding any other data,” he added. It is similarly difficult to ascertain the true number of Ukrainian soldiers killed fighting against Russia. Kyiv has been slightly more forthcoming, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy volunteering some estimates of battlefield losses in recent years, the latest in July putting the total at around 50,000 killed. But analysts say this is likely an undercount. An assessment by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies earlier this year said up to 150,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed, based on estimates from Britain’s military, Mediazona’s named war dead list, its own estimates and interviews with U.S., European, Ukrainian and other government officials.

articles.body: Before Americans reach for apple and pumpkin pies on Thanksgiving, they reach for another kind of pie the night before — one covered in sauce and cheese. Pizza was the most-ordered Thanksgiving Eve dinner on DoorDash last year, with orders up more than 50% compared with other Wednesdays in November, according to a new holiday report from the company. Cheese pizza orders rose 70%, Hawaiian pizza orders climbed 60% and pepperoni orders increased 50%, the report found. AMERICA'S BEST PIZZERIAS CROWNED IN NEW RANKINGS AS PIZZA EXPERT GIVES SLICE OF SKEPTICISM Thanksgiving Eve was also DoorDash's busiest Wednesday for restaurant orders for the second year in a row. Jeff Rinke of Hungry Howie's Pizza, a Michigan-born chain, said the night before Thanksgiving is typically one of the chain's strongest sales days, often rivaling Halloween and major sporting events. "Most people are preparing for Thanksgiving Day and want a quick and easy meal that everyone will enjoy," Rinke told Fox News Digital. "Kids are home from school and college students are back in town. More people are looking for quick, familiar food." At Arizona pizzeria Craft 64, owner James Swann said Thanksgiving Eve customers tend to order more, choose a wider variety and place orders further in advance than on a typical Wednesday. articles.title: PMQs: Kemi Badenoch challenges Andy Burnham over university fees for EU students
articles.summary: The PM says EU students paying the same as British students is the European position and "won't be put on the table".
articles.body:
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has challenged Andy Burnham over whether EU students in the UK could pay lower university tuition fees as part of his deal with the bloc.

The prime minister insisted the issue of tuition fees was "a separate deal", with discussions on this continuing.

Asked whether he could rule out EU students paying the same fees as British students, Burnham said this was "the European negotiating position" and "won't be put on the table".

A joint statement said they would also work towards a "supplementing" agreement on tuition fees for EU students in the UK and British students in the EU, with negotiations concluding within six months.

EU sources had earlier suggested the bloc might hold up applying the wider deal until it was agreed that EU students who wanted to study in the UK would pay the same fees as British students.

But the UK has insisted the wider deal will come into force regardless of whether the two sides can reach an agreement on tuition fees.

Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says

What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

At the moment, EU students at UK universities generally pay the same fees as international students, ranging from £11,400 to £38,000.

For British undergraduate students tuition fees are currently capped at £9,790 a year.

Universities have raised concerns that capping EU student fees at the same level could cost hundreds of millions a year, at a time when the sector is struggling financially.

At Prime Minister's Questions, Badenoch asked Burnham who would pick up the bill if EU and British students paid the same fees, "cash-strapped universities or cash-strapped taxpayers?"

In response, the PM said "the deal on tuition fees is not done", adding: "We will take that conversation forward always rightfully mindful of the challenges faced by higher education."

Pressed over whether the EU would still sign his wider deal if he refused to cut fees for European students, Burnham said legislation introduced in Parliament on Thursday would set a date for the implementation of deals on food, emissions and a youth experience scheme.

He added: "We will continue discussions with the European Union on the question of tuition fees."

Asked if he would rule out EU students paying the same tuition fees as British students, Burnham replied: "She is referring to the European negotiating position, which is not the British negotiating position.

"That has not been put on the table. It won't be put on the table."

Asked if Burnham was saying EU students would not pay domestic fees, the prime minister minister's official spokesman told reporters he would not get ahead of the outcome of ongoing talks.

articles.title: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
articles.summary: The Savasleyka airfield hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine.
articles.body:
Ukraine has said it damaged five Russian military aircraft in an attack on Russia's Savasleyka airfield, 300km (185 miles) east of Moscow.

Three MiG-31 and two Su-34s aircraft were hit, Kyiv's General Staff said, adding that the extent of the damage was still being assessed but that "there may be even better news to come". It did not elaborate on what weapons it had used to hit the airfield.

Russia has not commented on the strikes.

The airfield at Savasleyka, in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, has been a target for Ukraine for several years. It hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs.

The take-off of MiG-31s in particular frequently triggers nationwide alerts across Ukraine, as the Kinzhal missiles they carry have been known to hit large infrastructure and military targets and are difficult to shoot down.

Overnight, Kyiv also said it hit two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region some 800km (500 miles) from the front line – the latest in a series of long-range strikes which have dented Moscow's oil processing capacity.

"Did you repair them? We'll hit them again," the defence ministry in Kyiv said.

Samara region governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said the night-time attacks had been "a true ordeal", with more than 145 drones shot down. One person was killed and several towns experienced power outages, Fedorishchev said.

Kyiv also said it had hit a radar system as well as fuel and logistics depots across Ukrainian territories currently occupied by Russia.

"Without fuel, military vehicles cannot move; without ammunition, artillery falls silent," the defence ministry said, adding that every successful hit meant Moscow could carry out fewer strikes.

Kyiv has developed a thriving weapons industry and Ukrainian strikes on Russian targets well beyond the front line have become commonplace in the years since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion.

On Tuesday, President Vladimir Putin called for a tightening of security measures across the country's energy facilities.

But he also argued that Russia had managed to stabilise its domestic fuel market without suffering "critical damage" and added that Moscow would "inevitably" retaliate against Kyiv.

Ukraine continues to come under daily attack. Ten people were killed across several regions between 24 and 25 November, while thousands are without power after Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.
